clue.text: Crude metal with crude definition of copper to decrease?

parts.note: pig is a rude slang word for a police officer, a copper
to iron is to de-crease, taking the creases out of cloth

explanation.surface: A rough metal described alongside a rude name for a policeman who wants to cut something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to decrease' is read as 'to de-crease': ironing removes creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is the crude, impure metal that comes straight from a blast furnace.

clue.text: Fish, one established?

annotationWithheld.why: Fish, one established? (6): I (one) inside PLACE, but 'established' must supply both PLACE and the sense 'in place' that puts I inside, so one word does two jobs.

clue.text: One of six monarchs keen to get pregnant

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, stands for King George, and Britain has had six King Georges
avid means keen or eager

explanation.surface: One of a line of kings is eager to have an heir on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: GR (Georgius Rex) is the royal cipher of a King George; there have been six.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravid is a formal or medical word for carrying young, that is, pregnant.

clue.text: Leave a true drunk to make further judgement

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the words are staggering about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who walks out on a sober friend gets judged again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges LEAVE A TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-evaluate is to assess again, forming a fresh judgement.

clue.text: Scores are famous

definitions.meaning: musical scores are written down in notes, so a score is put into notation

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: musical scores are set down in notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means celebrated or well known, and a score is music recorded in notation.

clue.text: Weapon did its job on maiden

parts.note: a blade does its job when it cuts
a lass is a girl or maiden

explanation.surface: A weapon did its work on a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, the classic pirate weapon.

clue.text: Potential employee Frank had for breakfast

parts.note: frank means candid, honest and open
to have food for breakfast is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A man called Frank ate something for his breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone applying for a job, a possible future employee.

clue.text: Join up to make brass

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to abut is to join or border on something

explanation.surface: An instruction to join together to form a brass band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ABUT round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the largest, deepest instrument of the brass family.

clue.text: Bloody scene in a club with mob violence on the up

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

indicators.note: on the up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a riot is violence by a mob

explanation.surface: A gory scene where someone wields a club as mob violence grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' turns RIOT into TOIR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is literally a bloody place, where animals are killed for meat.

clue.text: Device which cuts grass ultimately to get neater

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word grass

parts.note: trimmer means neater or tidier

explanation.surface: A lawn gadget is meant to make the edges tidier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' seems to belong with 'cuts', but 'ultimately' takes only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A strimmer is a powered tool with a spinning line for cutting grass edges.

clue.text: Plant the first of acorns handed over

indicators.note: the first of picks out only the opening letter of the word acorns

parts.note: gave means handed over

explanation.surface: Someone planted the first acorn they were given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first of' takes A from 'acorns'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agave is a succulent plant of the Americas, source of tequila and sisal.

clue.text: Is he seen as somewhat dictatorial by nothing being given to the left?

definitions.text: Is he seen as somewhat dictatorial by nothing being given to the left?

indicators.note: letters given leftwards are read right to left, backwards
somewhat says only part of the run of words is taken

explanation.surface: A question whether a certain leader was regarded as a bit of a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' picks RIALBYNOT from 'dictatoRIAL BY NOThing', and 'being given to the left' reads it backwards. The whole clue doubles as a comment on the man.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Labour prime minister was often accused by critics of a presidential, controlling style.

clue.text: How to pay in terms of golf?

definitions.meaning: a way of paying by card, entering a code
two golf words: a short lofted shot and the flagstick on the green

explanation.walkthrough: A chip is a short lofted golf shot and the pin is the flagstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Chip and PIN is the card-payment system using a microchip and a personal number.

clue.text: One can tell automatically oxygen involved — it's basic

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an ATM, an automated teller machine, tells out cash automatically
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A machine spots the presence of oxygen and declares something fundamental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' puts O inside ATM. 'tell' is a bank teller, who counts out money.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the basic unit of matter, the fundamental building block of elements.

clue.text: Spooner's reason why mutton's off the menu, providing a more tender choice

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of the words are swapped, like the reverend's slips

parts.words: reason why mutton's off the menu
parts.note: there is no mutton if there is a lack of ram, a male sheep

parts.words: reason why mutton's off the menu
parts.note: there is no mutton if there is a lack of ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Mutton is off the menu, so diners get a more tender alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LACK OF RAM' with its first sounds swapped gives the dish; the B is silent so the swap is by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Rack of lamb is a prized cut of young sheep, far more tender than mutton.

clue.text: Blue public transporter in a state found in yellow stream

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: urine is the yellow stream

indicators.note: in means the tram goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: LA is the abbreviation for Louisiana, a US state
a tram is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A blue tram somewhere in America ends up in a yellow river.
explanation.walkthrough: LA is the standard abbreviation for Louisiana. 'yellow stream' is a jokey way of describing urine, though it reads like a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultramarine is a deep, vivid blue pigment originally made from lapis lazuli.

clue.text: Bomber's inaccuracy is featured in The Times initially

indicators.note: featured in means set inside, so these pieces go within the outer letters
initially takes the opening letter of each of the words The and Times

parts.note: an error is an inaccuracy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a bomber's mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bomber's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is just 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrorist may plant bombs, making 'bomber' an example of the type.

clue.text: Panda to cause shock eating one of four children

indicators.note: eating means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: to scar is to traumatise, causing lasting shock
a quad is one of quadruplets, four children born together

explanation.surface: A panda startles someone by devouring a child.
explanation.walkthrough: A Panda car was British slang for a small police patrol car, once painted in panda-like blue and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Panda car was the old British nickname for a police patrol car.

clue.text: Free from filth, it is mad?

annotationWithheld.why: Free from filth, it is mad? (8): a self-referential pun, 'it is mad' = 'it is in sane', IT IS inside SANE; 'mad' must give both SANE and the 'in' that places IT IS inside, so one word does two jobs, and the whole-phrase reverse reading is refused.
annotationWithheld.clue: Free from filth, it is mad?

clue.text: One suit for all the ship's officers

definitions.meaning: a pack of cards holds four suits, so one suit is a fourth of it
the officers of a ship collectively, named after their part of the deck

explanation.walkthrough: A deck of cards has four suits, so one suit is a quarter of the deck; 'for all' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The quarterdeck is the officers' area of a ship and, by extension, its officers as a body.

clue.text: Mad flier

explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is both a bird with a distinctive call and slang for crazy.

clue.text: Unfinished article interpreted as yarn

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
to read something is to interpret it

explanation.surface: A partly written article is taken to be a tall story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts THE to TH. 'yarn' looks like a story, but here it is spun fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread is a strand of spun fibre, which is what yarn is.

clue.text: Name of authors' family friends unfamiliar to the British

definitions.meaning: the surname of the novelists Kingsley and his son Martin
the French word for friends, foreign to British speakers

explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley and Martin, father and son, were both British novelists; 'amis' is French for friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Amis is the novelists' surname and the French plural for friends.

clue.text: Action taken by queen vacating throne that's on the cards

definitions.text: Action taken by queen vacating throne
definitions.meaning: what a monarch does on leaving the lavatory, the throne in slang
a poker hand, held in the cards

explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' is slang for a toilet, so a queen leaving it pulls the chain; the top poker hand is ace to ten of one suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal flush is the highest poker hand, ace, king, queen, jack and ten of a suit.

clue.text: A man's instrument

parts.note: taken as written
a gent is a man, a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man possesses a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' is used in its sense of a person acting for another.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument can be a person used to carry out another's will, as an agent is.

clue.text: Goddess offering wine to make man live

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a man
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A goddess pours wine to bring a man to life.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Hebe was cupbearer to the gods, serving their nectar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe, goddess of youth, served nectar to the Olympian gods as their cupbearer.

clue.text: Araucaria's indecipherable anagram to ignore letters of "bread"

indicators.note: anagram tells the solver to rearrange the letters of the word given
the letters of the word bread are left out of the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A puzzle by a famous setter whose rearrangement is impossible to crack without a bit of help.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B, R, E, A, D from INDECIPHERABLE, leaving INCIPHELE, and rearrange. Araucaria was also a much-loved Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the genus of the monkey puzzle tree, also called the Chilean pine.

clue.text: An animal turned, one turned painfully?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned means the word faces the other way, read backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer, an animal

explanation.surface: An animal wheels round and someone twists a joint in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives KLE from ELK; the definition plays on a twisted joint.
explanation.definitionFit: An ankle is the joint most often turned or sprained painfully.

clue.text: Once more bring in dance, twist etc

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

indicators.note: twist tells us to wrench the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of dances to bring back: reel, twist and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges ETC to ECT; the Twist looks like another dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elect is to vote someone into office again.

clue.text: Look into a proposal by model in the Sun, perhaps

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T
taken as written

indicators.note: into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bid is an offer or proposal
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Investigating a model's offer, as reported in a popular newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British popular newspaper; 'model' gives T from Ford's Model T car, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a British red-top tabloid, an example of this kind of newspaper.
